issues.title: [💡]: Pirate Hats & Headwear
issues.body:
### Your Suggestion

With the recent addition of the Plunder (pirate pillager) and other pirate-themed content, I think Supplementaries could take this theme even further by adding custom pirate hats and headwear.

Why this would be valuable:

- Currently, there are almost no high-quality pirate hat/headwear mods available on CurseForge (aside from one for 1.20.1).
- Supplementaries is known for delivering excellent sprites and 3D models, so it would be the first pirate hats with that level of polish.
- A dropped hat from the Plunder/Captain Pillager would be a fun and immersive reward, encouraging players to hunt them down while also making their loot table truly unique.
- This addition would fill a missing gap in the modding community, giving players the ability to roleplay or cosplay as iconic pirate characters (e.g., Gol D. Roger from One Piece).


### Extra Context

Additional suggestions: 
- Pirate hats as wearable items (cosmetic or with minor buffs).
- Captain Pillager drops his hat as rare loot.
- Potential variants (classic tricorn, bandana, feathered captain’s hat).

in a particular modpack i have, slingshots don't work; as in, blocks shot by one don't place. this happens even when the latest versions of supplementaries (1.20-3.1.43) and moonlight lib (1.20-2-16.36) are used and are the only mods present.

- [ ] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.20.1-FORGE

### Issue Details

Hello, I'm making a modpack and one of my custom structures has a Cannon from Supplementaries

The game deadlocks when the structure tries to generate

issues.body:

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

Details from a user suggests this:
Minecraft: 1.21.1
NeoForge: 21.1.252
DivineRPG: 1.10.10
Supplementaries: 1.21.1-3.9.9
DivineRPG Compatibility: 1.0.5

Problem:
DivineRPG and Supplementaries cause a class-initialization deadlock during parallel mod construction.

Thread 1:
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.configs.CommonConfigs.<clinit>
→ waiting for class initialization of:
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.configs.CommonConfigs$Building

Thread 2:
divinerpg.DivineRPG.<init>
→ divinerpg.registries.BlockRegistry.<clinit>
→ BlockRegistry.registerBlockSupplementariesRakedGravel
→ divinerpg.compat.supplementaries.SupplementariesLoader.rakedGravelEnabled
→ net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.configs.CommonConfigs$Building.<clinit>
→ waiting for class initialization of:
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.configs.CommonConfigs

This creates a circular class-init wait:

CommonConfigs
    waits for CommonConfigs$Building

CommonConfigs$Building
    is being accessed by DivineRPG's SupplementariesLoader
    and waits for CommonConfigs

NeoForge's ModLoader then waits indefinitely for the parallel mod-construction CompletableFuture.

Observed behavior:
DivineRPG ON + Supplementaries ON = hangs during Mod Construction
DivineRPG OFF + Supplementaries ON = boots
DivineRPG ON + Supplementaries OFF = boots

Changing/disabling the DivineRPG Supplementaries compatibility config did not prevent the deadlock.

Relevant DivineRPG method:
divinerpg.compat.supplementaries.SupplementariesLoader.rakedGravelEnabled()

Relevant Supplementaries classes:
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.configs.CommonConfigs
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.configs.CommonConfigs$Building

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.20.1-FABRIC

### Issue Details

Hello! I'm currently using Supplementaries 1.20-3.1.43 on Minecraft 1.20.1 Fabric, and I noticed a behavior with the Quiver's inventory interaction that can be quite inconvenient.

When holding arrows with the mouse cursor and right-clicking on a Quiver in the inventory, the arrows are inserted into the Quiver correctly. However, after the same click, the Quiver is also picked up by the mouse cursor.

This happens whether the Quiver is equipped in a Trinkets slot or simply placed in a normal inventory slot.

I'm not sure whether this behavior is intentional or not, but it makes the interaction somewhat inconvenient because the Quiver is automatically picked up after successfully inserting the arrows.

Steps to reproduce
Install Supplementaries 1.20-3.1.43 on Minecraft 1.20.1 Fabric.
Place a Supplementaries Quiver somewhere in the inventory.
Place some arrows in another inventory slot.
Pick up the arrows with the mouse cursor.
Move the cursor over the Quiver.
Right-click on the Quiver.
Actual behavior

The arrows are inserted into the Quiver correctly, but the Quiver is then picked up by the mouse cursor as part of the same interaction.

The same behavior occurs when the Quiver is equipped in a Trinkets slot.

Expected behavior

If this behavior is intentional, it would be helpful to have a configuration option to disable the Quiver being picked up after inserting arrows.

If it is not intentional, the interaction could instead be changed so that inserting arrows consumes the click and leaves the Quiver in its original inventory slot.

Additional information

The quiver_pickup configuration does not appear to control this behavior, as it concerns automatic arrow pickup rather than manual inventory interaction.

The issue can be reproduced even when the Quiver is not equipped in a Trinkets slot.

Environment
Minecraft: 1.20.1
Loader: Fabric
Supplementaries: 1.20-3.1.43
Moonlight Lib: 1.20-2.16.26
Trinkets: 3.7.2

### Logs & Media

issues.title: [1.21.1] 3.9.8: way sign structure search blocks the server thread (getChunk)
issues.body:
**Environment:** Supplementaries 1.21.1-3.9.8, Moonlight 3.3.3, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248, ~265 mods with heavy worldgen (a terrain overhaul, TerraBlender/Biolith, ~25 structure mods). Integrated server (singleplayer); the code path is server-side only, so a dedicated server should behave the same.

## What happens

When a village that carries way signs generates near the player, the server thread stops for 20-106 seconds: no block breaking, no interaction, entities frozen, and the usual

```
[Server thread/WARN] [net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer/]: Can't keep up! Is the server overloaded? Running 106636ms or 2132 ticks behind
```

I reproduced it five times in one session. Every freeze followed a

```
[pool-33-thread-4/INFO] [supplementaries/]: Searching for closest structure among [...] from position ...
```

line within a couple of seconds.

The cause is `BlockGeneratorBlockTile` running its structure search on a `CompletableFuture` from its own cached thread pool, and that search calling the blocking `LevelReader.getChunk(x, z, ChunkStatus.STRUCTURE_STARTS)`. `ServerChunkCache.getChunk` called from a non-server thread does not do the work on the caller: it schedules the load onto the server thread and blocks the caller until the chunk reaches the requested status. So the search is asynchronous only nominally — every candidate chunk whose structure start is not yet known is generated to `STRUCTURE_STARTS` **on the server thread**, one after another, while ticks wait behind it.

With a hardcoded radius of 250 chunks that is up to several hundred forced chunk generations per sign. On a vanilla-ish world each is cheap; in a pack where several mods hook worldgen at `STRUCTURE_STARTS` each costs tens to hundreds of milliseconds, which is where the multi-minute stalls come from. It is roughly the cost of a vanilla `/locate`, except it is triggered automatically by worldgen and overlaps with the chunk loading the player is already causing.

## Expected

Generating a way sign should not be able to stall the server thread. Either the search only consults structure starts the world already knows, or it is genuinely asynchronous (request the chunks without waiting and consult them on a later pass).

## Steps to reproduce

1. NeoForge 1.21.1 with Supplementaries 3.9.8 and a worldgen-heavy pack (terrain overhaul plus a couple of dozen structure mods).
2. Create a fresh world and travel into ungenerated terrain until a village with way signs generates.
3. Watch the log for `Searching for closest structure among [...]`; the server thread stalls within seconds and `Can't keep up!` follows.

A thread dump taken during the stall shows the pool thread blocked in `CompletableFuture.join` under `StructureLocator`, and the server thread in `ServerChunkCache.lambda$getChunk$0`.

## Evidence

Thread dumps of the stalls (358 samples over 12 minutes): of the 28 samples in which the server thread sat in `ServerChunkCache.getChunk -> managedBlock`, 21 were running the task `ServerChunkCache.lambda$getChunk$0`, i.e. a chunk request issued from another thread. That thread was `pool-33-thread-N`:

```
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture.join
net.minecraft.server.level.ServerChunkCache.getChunk
net.minecraft.world.level.Level.getChunk
net.minecraft.world.level.LevelReader.getChunk
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.common.worldgen.StructureLocator.getStructureThatWillSpawnAt
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.common.worldgen.StructureLocator.flushCandidates
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.common.worldgen.StructureLocator.findNearestStructures
net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.common.block.tiles.BlockGeneratorBlockTile.lambda$tick$0
java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture$AsyncSupply.run
```

Those dumps were taken on 3.8.9. Before filing this I checked that the code is unchanged in the current release: `BlockGeneratorBlockTile.class`, `StructureLocator.class`, `StructureLocator$StructureAndPlacement.class` and `LegacyStructureLocator.class` are **byte-for-byte identical (same sha1) in every release from 3.8.9 through 3.9.8**. Nothing in this path has been touched.

In 3.9.8's `StructureLocator.getStructureThatWillSpawnAt`, only `StructureCheckResult.START_NOT_PRESENT` short-circuits; `CHUNK_LOAD_NEEDED` falls straight through to the blocking `getChunk`:

```
  18: invokevirtual  StructureManager.checkStructurePresence
  25: getstatic      StructureCheckResult.START_NOT_PRESENT
  28: if_acmpeq      150            // -> return null
  ...
  73: getstatic      ChunkStatus.STRUCTURE_STARTS
  76: invokeinterface LevelReader.getChunk
```

The caller is unchanged as well. `BlockGeneratorBlockTile` still has `EXECUTORS = Executors.newCachedThreadPool()` in its static initialiser and still does `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(supplier, EXECUTORS)` in `tick`, and `lambda$tick$0` still passes a hardcoded search radius of 250 (`sipush 250`). Only `ROAD_SIGN_MAX_SEARCHES` and `ROAD_SIGN_EXIT_EARLY` are read from the config, so **no configuration setting can avoid this** — in particular `road_signs.max_search_radius` never reaches the way sign search.

No mixin in 3.9.8 targets either class, so nothing inside the mod alters this at runtime. The ten classes that reference them are ordinary call sites: `RoadSignFeature`, `AdventurerMapsHandler`, `CartographersQuillItem`, `BlockGeneratorBlock`, `ModRegistry`.

For context, the changelog entry for `1.21-3.5.0-neoforge` (2025-12-06), "improved the speed and accuracy of way sign and adventurer maps structure locations", looks like where the current `StructureLocator` came from.

## Suggested fix

In `getStructureThatWillSpawnAt`, never force generation from a pool thread. `StructureManager.checkStructurePresence` already tells you when generation would be needed, so treat `CHUNK_LOAD_NEEDED` the same way `START_NOT_PRESENT` is treated today:

```java
StructureCheckResult res = structureManager.checkStructurePresence(chunkPos, structure, ..., false);
if (res == StructureCheckResult.START_NOT_PRESENT || res == StructureCheckResult.CHUNK_LOAD_NEEDED) {
    return null;
}
```

and make the subsequent `getChunk` a memory-only lookup (`ChunkSource.getChunk(x, z, status, false)` / `getChunkNow`) so the pool thread can never block on chunk generation. The search then uses only structures the world already knows about, which is what a freshly generated village can realistically point at anyway.

If pointing into fully unexplored terrain matters, the candidate chunks could be requested through `ServerChunkCache.getChunkFuture` **without waiting** on them and consulted on a later tick pass — anything except a blocking `getChunk` from the pool.

I currently keep it off the server thread with a mixin in my pack that does exactly the first variant (skip `CHUNK_LOAD_NEEDED` candidates, serve `getChunk` from memory only). The freezes are gone and the signs still point at everything already generated. Happy to open a PR if that shape is acceptable.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

## Summary

When both **Supplementaries** and **Quark** are installed together, a **Cartographer villager located in the Nether** reliably crashes/disconnects the client the moment it levels up and rolls its "adventurer map" trade (Cartographer level 2). The client is kicked with:

```
Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException: Failed to encode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:merchant_offers'
Caused by: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException: Empty ItemStack not allowed
	at net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack$2.encode
	at net.minecraft.world.item.trading.MerchantOffer.writeToStream
```

This does **not** happen with either mod installed alone, and does **not** happen with Overworld cartographers — only Nether cartographers reproduce it. All mods and libraries are on the latest version for 1.21.1 Neoforge.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install both Supplementaries and Quark (default configs `quill_adventurer_maps` / `QUARK_QUILL` is `true` by default when Quark is present).
2. Spawn/find a Cartographer villager **in the Nether**.
3. Trade with it enough to level it up to level 2 (or otherwise trigger a trade-pool refresh at level 2), so it rolls Supplementaries' `supplementaries:adventurer_map` trade.
4. Client crashes with the encoder exception above and is disconnected. The server also then fails to persist that villager entity (`IllegalStateException: Value must be within range [1;99]: 0; Item must not be minecraft:air` while saving `AbstractVillager.addAdditionalSaveData`), confirming the corrupted `MerchantOffer` was actually written into the villager's trade list, not just a one-off encode glitch.

**Confirmed with an isolated test:** reproduced this crash in a minimal setup with *only* Quark, Supplementaries, and their own required dependencies (Moonlight, Zeta) installed. Same exact stack trace (`Failed to encode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:merchant_offers'` → `Empty ItemStack not allowed`).

issues.title: [🐞]: AbstractRopeKnotBlock#getShape/getCollisionShape: unprotected getBlockEntity() call can throw uncaught off-thread
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/Connector etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [ ] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

## Summary

`AbstractRopeKnotBlock#getShape` (and `#getCollisionShape`) call `BlockGetter#getBlockEntity(pos)` unprotected, one line before the existing `try/catch` that's meant to guard against exactly this kind of failure. When `getShape()`/`getCollisionShape()` is invoked off the main server thread (e.g. by the light engine during a light update) for a chunk that cannot be synchronously created in that context, `getBlockEntity()` throws an uncaught `IllegalStateException`. On our server this exception killed a light-engine worker mid-task, which left the chunk it was processing in a state where whatever was awaiting its future never got signaled — resulting in a full server hang and a forced `ServerHangWatchdog` crash a short time later.

## Environment

- Minecraft: 1.21.1
- NeoForge: 21.1.248
- Supplementaries: `1.21.1-3.8.9` (neoforge)
- Also present: Moonlight Lib (required dependency)

## The bug

`net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/common/block/blocks/AbstractRopeKnotBlock.java`, `getShape(BlockState, BlockGetter, BlockPos, CollisionContext)`:

```java
@Override
public VoxelShape getShape(BlockState state, BlockGetter world, BlockPos pos, CollisionContext context) {
    if (world.getBlockEntity(pos) instanceof RopeKnotBlockTile tile) {   // <-- NOT covered by the try/catch below
        try {
            return tile.getShape();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            Supplementaries.LOGGER.error("Failed to get block shape for rope knot block at {}", pos);
        }
    }
    return super.getShape(state, world, pos, context);
}
```

`world.getBlockEntity(pos)` is the call on the `if` line — it is outside the `try` block, so any exception it throws propagates uncaught. We confirmed via `javap -c` against the real compiled 1.21.1-3.8.9 class that `getCollisionShape(BlockState, BlockGetter, BlockPos, CollisionContext)` has the exact same pattern (identical unprotected `invokeinterface` to `BlockGetter.getBlockEntity` before its own `try`).

Both methods are on the hot path for collision checks and light propagation, meaning they can legitimately be invoked from threads other than the main server thread (in our case, from `ThreadedLevelLightEngine`'s worker pool during `BlockLightEngine.propagateIncrease`).

## Observed exception

```
[Worker-Main-20/ERROR] [minecraft/Util]: Caught exception in thread Thread[#241,Worker-Main-20,5,main]
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Should always be able to create a chunk!
	at net.minecraft.world.level.Level.getChunk(Level.java:204)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.Level.getChunk(Level.java:5825)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.Level.getChunkAt(Level.java:5820)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.Level.getBlockEntity(Level.java:777)
	at net.mehvahdjukaar.supplementaries.common.block.blocks.AbstractRopeKnotBlock.getShape(AbstractRopeKnotBlock.java:126)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase.getShape(BlockBehaviour.java:650)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase.getShape(BlockBehaviour.java:646)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour.propagatesSkylightDown(BlockBehaviour.java:382)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase.propagatesSkylightDown(BlockBehaviour.java:518)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour.getLightBlock(BlockBehaviour.java:296)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase.getLightBlock(BlockBehaviour.java:522)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.lighting.LightEngine.getOpacity(LightEngine.java:82)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.lighting.BlockLightEngine.propagateIncrease(BlockLightEngine.java:58)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.lighting.LightEngine.propagateIncreases(LightEngine.java:177)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.lighting.LightEngine.runLightUpdates(LightEngine.java:157)
	at net.minecraft.world.level.lighting.LevelLightEngine.runLightUpdates(LevelLightEngine.java:53)
	at net.minecraft.server.level.ThreadedLevelLightEngine.runUpdate(ThreadedLevelLightEngine.java:185)
	at net.minecraft.server.level.ThreadedLevelLightEngine.lambda$tryScheduleUpdate$27(ThreadedLevelLightEngine.java:164)
	at net.minecraft.util.thread.ProcessorMailbox.pollTask(ProcessorMailbox.java:91)
	at net.minecraft.util.thread.ProcessorMailbox.pollUntil(ProcessorMailbox.java:146)
	at net.minecraft.util.thread.ProcessorMailbox.run(ProcessorMailbox.java:102)
	at java.util.concurrent.ForkJoinTask$RunnableExecuteAction.compute(ForkJoinTask.java:1750)
	at java.util.concurrent.ForkJoinPool.runWorker(ForkJoinPool.java:2019)
	at java.util.concurrent.ForkJoinWorkerThread.run(ForkJoinWorkerThread.java:187)
```

This happened on a modded server (list of other mods available on request; none of them touch `AbstractRopeKnotBlock` or this code path directly). The exception itself was only logged, not fatal by itself — but a server hang (`ServerHangWatchdog` force-kill, single tick reported as taking 60000000+ ms) followed roughly a minute later. We can't prove 100% causally that this exact exception is what caused that specific hang (we were mid-investigation of an unrelated, separate chunk-loading issue involving other mods), but the mechanism is real and reproducible regardless: an uncaught exception on a light-engine worker thread, triggered by a rope knot block sitting near a chunk that isn't in a state to be synchronously created, is not something that should ever be allowed to escape `getShape()`/`getCollisionShape()`.

## Suggested fix

Move `world.getBlockEntity(pos)` inside the existing `try` block (or wrap it separately), the same way `tile.getShape()`/`tile.getCollisionShape()` are already protected, e.g.:

```java
@Override
public VoxelShape getShape(BlockState state, BlockGetter world, BlockPos pos, CollisionContext context) {
    try {
        if (world.getBlockEntity(pos) instanceof RopeKnotBlockTile tile) {
            return tile.getShape();
        }
    } catch (Exception e) {
        Supplementaries.LOGGER.error("Failed to get block shape for rope knot block at {}", pos);
    }
    return super.getShape(state, world, pos, context);
}
```

(and the equivalent change in `getCollisionShape`).

We wrote a small standalone Mixin (`@Redirect` on the `getBlockEntity` call in both methods, falling back to `null` on exception) as a stopgap for our own server, verified against the compiled 1.21.1-3.8.9 bytecode. Happy to share it if useful as a reference, though a proper fix upstream would obviously be preferable.


### Logs & Media

[error.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31282088/error.txt)

issues.title: [🐞]: Bamboo Spikes and Tipped Bamboo Spikes share the same block, causing `Block.asItem()` to resolve to the wrong item
issues.body: ### Mandatory Troubleshooting - [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher. - [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/Connector etc). - [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already. - [x] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod. ### Minecraft Version & Loader 1.21.1-NEOFORGE ### Issue Details **Description:** Both `BAMBOO_SPIKES_ITEM` and `BAMBOO_SPIKES_TIPPED_ITEM` are registered as `BlockItem` subclasses using the same `BAMBOO_SPIKES` block reference: ```java BAMBOO_SPIKES_ITEM = regItem("bamboo_spikes", () -> new BlockItem(BAMBOO_SPIKES.get(), ...)) BAMBOO_SPIKES_TIPPED_ITEM = regItem("bamboo_spikes_tipped", () -> new BambooSpikesTippedItem(BAMBOO_SPIKES.get(), new Item.Properties() .component(DataComponents.POTION_CONTENTS, new PotionContents(Potions.POISON)) .component(ModComponents.CHARGES.get(), 16))) ``` `BambooSpikesTippedItem extends BlockItem`, so both constructors register into vanilla's `Item.BY_BLOCK` map using the same block key. Since `BAMBOO_SPIKES_TIPPED_ITEM` is constructed second, it overwrites that mapping — meaning `BAMBOO_SPIKES.asItem()` / `new ItemStack((ItemLike) BAMBOO_SPIKES.get())` resolves to the tipped item (with its default Poison + 16 charges state) instead of the plain spike item. **Observed symptom:** In `SpecialRecipeDisplays.makeSpikeRecipe()`, the line: ```java ItemStack spikes = new ItemStack((ItemLike)ModRegistry.BAMBOO_SPIKES.get()); ``` intends to create a plain Bamboo Spikes stack for the recipe-viewer display, but instead produces a Poison Tipped Bamboo Spikes stack (16 charges) due to the above collision. This shows up in JEI/EMI as every "Tipped Bamboo Spikes" display recipe (for every potion variant) incorrectly listing a Poison Tipped Bamboo Spikes as an ingredient instead of the plain Bamboo Spikes, and EMI's fill-crafting-grid function inserts the same wrong item. **Note:** Manual crafting via the actual crafting table works correctly, since `TippedBambooSpikesRecipe.matches()` checks against `BAMBOO_SPIKES_ITEM` directly rather than going through `Block.asItem()`. ### Logs & Media

issues.title: [💡]: Tattered Book & Quill
issues.body:
### Your Suggestion

Simply put, a way to turn a Book & Quill into a Tattered variant using Antique Ink with the same font and layout would be very nice.

### Extra Context

One of the biggest issues right now is that if you've written too much, or formatted your book like you would normally, then converting it over to a tattered one will ruin the formatting and can sometimes remove text entirely if it runs on for too long. Being able to write in this font and be able would fix this issue and make it far easier to format your books for the Tattered format, since you'd actually be writing in the same font style.

issues.title: [🐞]: Sacks dont work as expected in Dispensers
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/Connector etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [x] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

Sacks do not behave like other dispensible entities. Shulker boxes, minecarts, and boats all check to see if a tile entity is in the space they try to dispense into, if so rather then dropping the item they retain it. This behavior is extremly valuable for things like loading items into them. Since Sacks dont do this check, attempting to dispense will throw it on the ground making it significalty more complicated to make a system that auto loads items into it then breaking it.

Easily replicatable by placing a sack in a dispenser, then triggering it while any tile entity is in front of it.

issues.title: [🐞]: Unmarked incompatibility/dependency with NeoForge Versions below 21.1.221
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/Connector etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [ ] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

After updating parts of my custom modpack, I discovered that pistons firing led to an immediate CTD.
Checking the latest logs, it appears the culprit was an outdated version of spongepowered.mixins.
NeoForge 21.1.220 only has version 0.5, rather than the 0.5.3 that Supplementaries calls on.
Disabling Supplementaries' piston tweaks did not resolve this, either.

Thankfully, updating the the immediate next version fixed my issue, but I can't exactly blindly update to the latest version since that can cause other incompatibilities, and this dependency also seems poorly documented on NeoForge's end (accessing changelogs for versions other than the current Minecraft version doesn't seem intended).

With NeoForge 21.1.221, pistons now work as they should again. No fix needed on your end, but you might want to set a dependency.
Can't upload the full log, sadly. Let me know if you need more than an excerpt.

issues.title: [🐞]: Conflict with MoreVillagers
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/Connector etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [x] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

There seems to be a conflict with MoreVillagers that started in the 3.7.7 version for 1.21.1 on Neoforge. 

Some of the villagers from that mod when, getting to their tier 3 or 4 trades (specifically the enderologist tier 4 trades is what I was testing with) calls for air as an item and causes a crash or Neruina error if villager is in an easy villagers trader, when trying to open their trades. Removing this mod or playing on the 3.6.7 version allows them to work normally. 

I know this isn't the most recent version (but it's the most recent one compatible in the pack I'm playing) but I didn't see it reported as an issue so figured it was worth mentioning in case it's still hanging around.

### Logs & Media

[latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30482645/latest.log)

issues.title: Crash with sodium 0.8.12 alpha 4 on neoforge 1.21.1 when entering a world
issues.body:
Hi!

I've encountered a crash when entering a world. The game reaches the main menu normally, but crashes immediately when loading into a singleplayer world.

Environment
Minecraft: 1.21.1
Loader: NeoForge 21.1.233
Supplementaries: 1.21.1-3.6.7

[crash-2026-06-13_14.47.51-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28910040/crash-2026-06-13_14.47.51-client.txt)

Sodium: 0.8.12-alpha.4+mc1.21.1
Description

The game launches successfully and reaches the main menu. The crash only occurs during world loading, when Sodium initializes the world renderer.

The crash report points to a failed mixin injection from Supplementaries:

CompatSodiumFluidRendererMixin from mod supplementaries failed injection check
Scanned 0 target(s)

and occurs while Sodium is constructing:

net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.neoforge.render.FluidRendererImpl
Relevant Exception
org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InjectionError:
Critical injection failure:
CompatSodiumFluidRendererMixin
from mod supplementaries
failed injection check,
(0/1) succeeded.
Scanned 0 target(s).
Additional Notes

This appears to be related to Sodium compatibility code rather than world content itself, as the crash happens before the world finishes loading.

Full crash report attached.

Thanks for taking a look!

issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Issue Details

Hello! I am experiencing a critical crash on startup. The game throws a Mixin injection failure related to fluid rendering compatibility between the native NeoForge versions of Supplementaries and Sodium.

### Environment
* **Minecraft:** 1.21.1
* **Mod Loader:** NeoForge 21.1.230
* **Supplementaries:** 1.21.1-3.6.5 (NeoForge)
* **Sodium:** 0.8.12-alpha.2+mc1.21.1 (NeoForge)

### Crash Details
The crash occurs at `CompatSodiumFluidRendererMixin`. It seems the `supplementaries$modifyLumiseneEmissivity` method is failing to find its target callback in the newer Sodium NeoForge version (0.8.12).

**Error snippet:**
`org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InjectionError: Critical injection failure: Callback method supplementaries$modifyLumiseneEmissivity(...) in supplementaries.mixins.json:compat.CompatSodiumFluidRendererMixin from mod supplementaries failed injection check, (0/1) succeeded.`

issues.title: [🗃]: Compatibility with modern Sodium 0.8.12 alpha backports to 1.21.1
issues.body:
Hi,
I'm a maintainer on Sodium and today we published the first alpha from our graduated backport experiment. This means that we [now have Sodium 0.8.12 on 1.21.1](https://modrinth.com/mod/sodium/versions?c=alpha&g=1.21.1). You can find more information about this [in our blog post on discord](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/1077645005042233374/1501010160326414426).

We've since noticed Supplementaries interacting with Sodium and crashing on world load. In particular it appears your `CompatSodiumFluidRendererMixin` is failing here. The gist is that since 0.8.x includes many changes to various parts of Sodium, including our new Config API, mods such as this one will encounter breakage when users (cluelessly) update modpacks with the latest published versions.

If you'd like to coordinate more closely with us, you're invited to [our discord server.](https://caffeinemc.net/discord) I intend for this to be considered a "feature" since this software is currently in alpha and not the mainline release. A lack of compatibility is not a fault on your part, but rather I would just like to notify you of the situation. I hope this doesn't cause too much trouble!

I've made this issue in addition to the [user report](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/supplementaries/issues/2009) to point out some general information. You are of course free to close and/or otherwise handle this issue as you please.

Thanks!

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.

issues.title: [🐞]: Mixin conflict in CompatEMFMixin breaking EMF model loading
issues.body:
### Mandatory Troubleshooting

- [x] Use the LATEST version of the mod and ALL its dependencies (or ideally all your mods). Pro tip: don't install mods manually, use a launcher.
- [x] Don't use Optifine or hybrid servers (Mohist/Velocity/etc) and have tried without big game altering mods (Sodium/Lithium/Connector etc).
- [x] Check that this bug hasn't been reported already.
- [x] Try with the mod alone. If issue does not persist then try removing half of your mods at the time to find the conflicting mod.

### Minecraft Version & Loader

1.21.1-FABRIC

### Issue Details

## Deets
Minecraft Version: 1.21.1
Mod Loader: Fabric 0.18.6
Supplementaries Version: 1.21-3.5.34-fabric
Entity Model Features (EMF) Version: 3.2.2

## The Problem
When launching the game with both Supplementaries and Entity Model Features installed, EMF is unable to load any custom entity models. I get spammed with `default model returned` warnings which I think stem from a Mixin transformation failure caused by `supplementaries-common.mixins.json:compat.CompatEMFMixin`.

It appears EMF recently changed a method signature in `EMFModelPartCustom` that Supplementaries is trying to inject into (`onInit`), adding an `EMFModelPartRoot` parameter which causes an `Invalid descriptor` exception.

## Error Snippet
```log
Mixin apply for mod supplementaries failed supplementaries-common.mixins.json:compat.CompatEMFMixin from mod supplementaries -> traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartCustom: org.spongepowered.asm.mixin.injection.throwables.InvalidInjectionException Invalid descriptor
```

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install Supplementaries (`1.21-3.5.26`) and EMF (`3.2.2`) on Fabric 1.21.1.
2. Launch the client.
3. Observe the massive console spam as EMF fails to apply models, citing the Supplementaries mixin failure.

  Moonlight Lib 1.21-2.29.33

I have verified that the crash does not occur with only Supplementaries or Quark alone. 
With both mods installed, the game crashes within seconds of flying into the West direction.

I first encountered this in a small self-made pack with no other mods that change The End world generation. I narrowed down the modlist from there to produce this minimum example, though the crash manifests differently with these steps to reproduce as with my modpack's singleplayer world. issues.title: [1.21.1 NeoForge] NPE crash when Plunderer AI computes cannon trajectory (fake ItemRightClickEvent + YAWP)
issues.body:
### Environment
- **Minecraft**: 1.21.1
- **NeoForge**: 21.1.221
- **Supplementaries**: 1.21-3.5.34-neoforge
- **Moonlight**: latest
- **Conflicting mod**: YAWP (Yet Another World Protection) `yawp-1.21.1-neoforge-0.6.2-beta1`
- **Side**: Dedicated server crash (Ticking entity)

### Description

The server crashes on a Plunderer entity ticking. Root chain:

1. `UseCannonBlockGoal#tick` → `PlundererAICommon#aimCannonAndShoot`
2. `PlundererAICommon#setCannonAnglesToFollowTrajectory` → `CannonBlockTile#setChanged` → `recomputeTrajectoryData`
3. `computeTrajectoryData` → `AlternativeBehavior#calculateData` → `GenericProjectileBehavior#calculateData` → `GenericProjectileBehavior#createEntity`
4. `SuppPlatformStuffImpl#fireItemRightClickEvent` fires a **synthetic** `PlayerInteractEvent.RightClickItem` during trajectory simulation
5. YAWP's `PlayerFlagHandler#onEntityInteraction` listener runs the fake event and NPEs because the region data for this dimension isn't initialized:

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "de.z0rdak.yawp.data.region.LevelRegionData.getLocalList()"
because the return value of "de.z0rdak.yawp.data.region.RegionDataManager.getOrCreate(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation)"
is null
```

### Why this is (likely) on Supplementaries' side

`GenericProjectileBehavior#createEntity` fires a real `ItemRightClickEvent` from an AI tick context — no actual player right-click, no actual hand interaction. Other event listeners (YAWP, and probably a few griefing-prevention mods) assume this event only fires from a real player interaction and can therefore NPE or misbehave.

### Minimal repro
1. Install Supplementaries + YAWP on a dedicated server (NeoForge 1.21.1).
2. Place a cannon + spawn a Plunderer (or wait for a plunderer patrol).
3. Plunderer targets a player/cannon → ticks → crash.

### Full stack (shortened)
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "LevelRegionData.getLocalList()" because the return value of "RegionDataManager.getOrCreate(ResourceLocation)" is null
    at yawp/RegionDataManager.getLocalsFor(RegionDataManager.java:298)
    at yawp/FlagEvaluator.getInvolvedRegionsFor(FlagEvaluator.java:228)
    at yawp/FlagEvaluator.evaluate(FlagEvaluator.java:146)
    at yawp/PlayerFlagHandler.onEntityInteraction(PlayerFlagHandler.java:729)
    at neoforge/CommonHooks.onItemRightClick(CommonHooks.java:806)
    at supplementaries/SuppPlatformStuffImpl.fireItemRightClickEvent(SuppPlatformStuffImpl.java:198)
    at supplementaries/GenericProjectileBehavior.createEntity(GenericProjectileBehavior.java:124)
    at supplementaries/GenericProjectileBehavior.calculateData(GenericProjectileBehavior.java:34)
    at supplementaries/AlternativeBehavior.calculateData(AlternativeBehavior.java:27)
    at supplementaries/CannonBlockTile.computeTrajectoryData(CannonBlockTile.java:229)
    at supplementaries/CannonBlockTile.recomputeTrajectoryData(CannonBlockTile.java:303)
    at supplementaries/CannonBlockTile.setChanged(CannonBlockTile.java:222)
    at supplementaries/PlundererAICommon.setCannonAnglesToFollowTrajectory(PlundererAICommon.java:103)
    at supplementaries/PlundererAICommon.aimCannonAndShoot(PlundererAICommon.java:63)
    at supplementaries/UseCannonBlockGoal.tick(UseCannonBlockGoal.java:181)
```

### Suggested fix

Avoid firing `ItemRightClickEvent` during trajectory **simulation**. The call in `GenericProjectileBehavior#createEntity` (line 124) only needs to construct an entity to predict its flight path — there's no actual player interaction happening. Options:

1. **Skip the event call** when the context is a trajectory prediction (guard with a "simulation" flag passed into `createEntity`).
2. **Use a null-checked internal path** that instantiates the projectile without going through `ItemStack#use`/`Item#use` / the event chain.
3. If the event chain really must run, wrap the call in try/catch and fall back to a default trajectory, so a misbehaving listener can't crash the AI.

Option 1 or 2 is preferable since it removes the surface area entirely.

### Context

The crash also surfaces a pre-existing YAWP bug (`RegionDataManager.getOrCreate` returning null should never cause an NPE downstream), but Supplementaries is the trigger by firing the event from a non-player AI path. Happy to cross-report on YAWP's repo once this side is acknowledged.

issues.title: [🗃]: Potentially include `#c:relocation_not_supported` in `supplementaries:unrotatable`
issues.body:
This is a personal thing that I have done in my modpack *just in case*, but I just thought I could bring it up here for further discussion, as well.

The tag `supplementaries:unrotatable`, which prevents some blocks from being rotated by a **Turntable** or **Wrench**, has quite a few inclusions. These exist either because the ability to rotate them willy-nilly would be overpowered, break the block's functionality, or both.

https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/88e6ccbbd48bd6089d00fca3737c19fb72e0d26d/common/src/main/resources/data/supplementaries/tags/block/un_rotatable.json#L1-L23

I would suggest this tag to also implicitly include `#c:relocation_not_supported`, as the tag almost always includes blocks that break under similar conditions (e.g. `create:track`).

The problem worthy of discussion is... semantics. For reference, the [NeoForge documentation](https://lexxie.dev/neoforge/1.21.1/net/neoforged/neoforge/common/Tags.Blocks.html#RELOCATION_NOT_SUPPORTED) clearly states:
> Blocks should be included in this tag if their movement/relocation can cause serious issues such as world corruption upon being moved or for balance reason where the block should not be able to be relocated.

"*Relocation*" is not the same as "*rotation*", but in Minecraft it kind of is, as both require changing block states. While it makes sense to me, it's a tough sell.

issues.title: [🐞]: Easter egg freezes the client for multiple seconds when rendering a doormat for the first time
issues.body:
### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed the steps above.

### Minecraft Version

1.20.1-FABRIC

### Supplementaries Version

supplementaries-1.20-3.1.41

### Describe the Issue

Never in my life had I thought I'd file an issue like this. You got a laugh out of me when I figured out what's going wrong.

Walk with me through the issue:

1. The first time a doormat is rendered, the `TextUtils` class is initialized. A doormat is not required, strictly speaking, e.g. a notice board works too, but a doormat is more common.
2. The `static` initializer for `TextUtils` includes the script of the Bee Movie and pre-renders it via `Minecraft.getInstance().font.split(TextUtil.parseText(b, null), Mth.floor(lx * SCALING_FACTOR))`.
3. `font.split` is `TextRendered.wrapLines` in Loom mappings (forgive me for using those), which takes a `StringVisitable` argument and forwards it to `TextHandler.wrapLines`.
4. `TextHandler.wrapLines` has multiple overloads. We're interested in the two most similar ones, where the first one takes any `StringVisitable` object, and the second specializes for `String`. Since we're in a generic context (and `FormattedText` is not a `String` anyway), the generic implementation is invoked.
5. While the `String`-specific implementation contains some clever logic to efficient split the string into lines, the generic implementation is stupid and just splits offs lines one by one and keeps the tail. This has quadratic time complexity, so it already has a chance to freeze.
6. For whatever reason, it seems like this doesn't actually freeze the client for a noticeable time. Maybe it's just short, or maybe JVM optimizes this somehow, I have no clue. But the moment you add any mod for text formatting to the mix, e.g. [Inline](https://github.com/SamsTheNerd/inline), which I originally reproduced this bug with, these long tails become visible to external code.
7. Now, for each rendered line, the entire remainder of the string is sent to Inline, which runs regular expressions on it. Since the total length of the lines is very large, this hangs the client for about 10 seconds.
8. Notably, this would not happen had Minecraft used a smarter splitting algorithm, or Supplementaries invoked `wrapLines` with a `String`, going through `TextHandler`, instead of invoking it with `StringVisitable`.

The alternative of asking Mojang to fix their code aside, I think the only reasonable solution here is to remove the two formatting codes in the bee movie text and invoke `wrapLines` with a raw string.

issues.title: [🐞]: Cog blocks provide signal strength 1 lower than expected
issues.body: ### Confirmation - [x] I have read and followed the steps above. ### Minecraft Version 1.21.1-NEOFORGE ### Supplementaries Version supplementaries-1.21-3.5.27-neoforge ### Describe the Issue When powering other redstone components, cog blocks provide power 1 lower than their current `power`. This leads to `power:1` cog blocks not powering adjacent blocks, and comparators reading 1 lower than the power of a given cog block. ### For power 1: - Place a redstone power source such as a redstone block, then connect a line of 15 cog blocks such that when targeting the last block the debug menu shows `power:1`. - Place a redstone component such as a dispenser or redstone lamp such that it is adjacent to the `power:1` block and no other cog blocks. - Observe that the redstone component does not receive power from the cog block. ### For other strengths: - Place a solid, redstone-conducting block such as wool. - Attach a crank to the wool block, set it to at least signal strength 2. - Place a cog block adjacent to the wool block, with a comparator reading from the cog block - Place a redstone dust on the output of the comparator - observe that the signal strength of the dust is one level lower than the strength of the crank. I think this behavior is due to the following line in `CogBlock.java`: https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/7e851b36962fb8e53fecb29a815a3ebfb943f1b2/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/common/block/blocks/CogBlock.java#L50 I think this is how cog blocks implement signal strength decay, but since the subtraction happens in the `getSignal` method, every component sees one signal strength lower instead of the (I assume) intended behavior of only dust and other cog blocks seeing the lower signal strength. The current behavior prevents infinite-length instant wires using alternating dust and cog blocks, which I think is desirable and would guess to be intentional, therefore I wasn't sure whether to post this as a question or bug. I chose to post it as a bug since the strength 1 behavior is unexpected. The closest issue I could find regarding cog blocks was the closed issue https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/issues/314, which is different to the behavior stated here. Interestingly, duplicating the setup shown in this issue demonstrates that two cog blocks both reporting `power:15` can provide different signal strengths to adjacent redstone devices. A cog block directly powered by a repeater, torch, comparator or dust will power an adjacent cog block to the same level, but the second cog block will output a signal strength 1 lower to any adjacent components. For example, both cog blocks show `power:15` in the debug menu. My understanding is that the vanilla "opaque block" behavior is overriding the cog block behavior. Mods: NeoForge v.21.1.219 moonlight-1.21-2.29.20-neoforge supplementaries-1.21-3.5.27-neoforge

issues.title: [🐞]: Flickering dots while holding torches with Dynamic Lights
issues.body: ### Confirmation - [x] I have read and followed the steps above. ### Minecraft Version 1.21.1-FABRIC ### Supplementaries Version supplementaries-1.21-3.5.24-fabric.jar ### Describe the Issue When using Supplementaries together with Dynamic Lights (both LambDynamicLights and Sodium Dynamic Lights), holding a torch can produce small flickering dots above it that jitter with camera movement. In a minimal environment (only Dynamic Lights + Supplementaries): A red dot appears and disappears as you move the camera. The effect is subtle but still present. More noticeable when looking out into the distance. In a full modded environment: The glitch is much more obvious. Multiple orange dots appear and flicker. Enabling True Darkness makes the effect more visible, especially at night. Disabling Supplementaries completely removes the glitch, True Darkness or not. Steps to reproduce: Install: Dynamic Lights (LambDynamicLights or Sodium Dynamic Lights, latest version) Supplementaries (latest version) True Darkness (amplifies visibility) Hold a torch in your hand. Move the camera while looking around the world. Observe flickering dots above the torch. Expected behavior: Torches should dynamically light the world without producing any floating/flickering dots. Observed behavior: Minimal environment: subtle red dot flickers while moving the camera. Full mod environment: multiple orange dots flicker and are very noticeable. True Darkness amplifies the effect. Disabling Supplementaries removes the issue. Environment: Minecraft: [1.21.1] Loader: [Fabric-0.18.4] Mods: Dynamic Lights + Supplementaries (+ optionally True Darkness) Additional info: Screenshot provided, though the dots are subtle and hard to see. The issue seems to be caused by Supplementaries’ interaction with Dynamic Lights’ torch rendering, not Dynamic Lights itself. This screenshot was taken in a full modded environment since its easier to capture while standing still, in a minimal environment it mostly only happens with camera movement and jitters around the screen instead of staying still.

### Version

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Supplementaries Version

1.21-3.5.19

### Moonlight Lib Version

1.21-2.29.16

### Describe Issue

When a player dies while chat is open, the game crashes and disconnects them with a `NullPointerException: Screen cannot be null` originating from Forgified Fabric API's `ScreenEvents.remove()`. The crash is triggered through Supplementaries' `ClientPacketListenerMixin` injecting into `handlePlayerCombatKill`.

This has been reproduced 100% of the time with only the three mods listed below, no other mods are required to trigger it.


## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Minecraft | 1.21.1 |
| Loader | NeoForge 21.1.x |
| Supplementaries | 1.21-3.5.19 **(NeoForge native version)** |
| Moonlight Lib | 1.21-2.29.16 |
| Forgified Fabric API | 0.116.7+2.2.3+1.21.1 |

> This is the **native NeoForge build** of Supplementaries — Sinytra Connector is **not** involved and is **not** required to reproduce this crash.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Replicate the environment above (only 3 mods)
2. Join a world or server.
3. Die with chat open. E.g,
```
/effect give @s minecraft:instant_damage infinite
```
and open chat immediately after.

**Result:** Client crashes with the error below and the player is disconnected.  
**Expected:** Player sees the death screen normally.

[Relevant Error Snippet](https://gist.github.com/abb3v/7fb0a55ec21f99d9ae1193605f99cad1)

### Describe Issue

Hello,
I am experiencing a server-side crash on startup when using newer versions of Moonlight Library. The same server starts correctly when using an older Moonlight version.

The crash happens during ServerStartedEvent, when Moonlight attempts to create a FakeServerLevel.

Environment

Minecraft: 1.20.1

Environment: Server

Moonlight Library:

❌ Fails: 2.16.x

✅ Works: 2.14.x

Supplementaries:

❌ Fails together with newer Moonlight versions

Java: 17

Crash details

This is a NullPointerException, not a watchdog or performance-related issue.

Relevant stacktrace excerpt:

java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke 
"WorldInfoBridge.bridge$setWorld(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel)"
because an internal world reference is null

at net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel.<init>
at net.mehvahdjukaar.moonlight.core.misc.FakeServerLevel.<init>
at net.mehvahdjukaar.moonlight.core.misc.FakeServerLevel$DummyServerChunkCache.<init>
at net.mehvahdjukaar.moonlight.core.misc.FakeLevelManager.getServer


The server crashes immediately during startup.

Important notes

The issue only happens on the server

Older Moonlight versions work correctly in the same setup

This is not a tick freeze or watchdog issue

Increasing max-tick-time or using Spark does not apply here

Expected behavior

The server should start normally, as it does with older Moonlight versions.

Additional info

It appears that newer Moonlight versions initialize FakeServerLevel in a way that triggers a null reference during server startup.

I can provide the full crash report and exact tested versions if needed.

Thank you for your time.

issues.title: [🗃]:Disabling Sack Tooltips in Config
issues.body:
Seeing your code, it looks like you're manually checking if the user is using Quark Shulker preview feature or Shulker Box Tooltips to disable the Sack tooltips.

However, I'm using a datapack to add them as Easy Shulker Boxes containers, to achieve the same effect (as well as using them like Bundles).

As this use case can not be easily be taken into account via manual compat, would it be possible for you to add a Config option to disable the Sack Tooltips ?

Additionnally, I could give you the datapack if you wanted to have a manual compat, but I understand if this is not something you wish to pursue !

Thank you for your time !

I cannot load into any world without being kicked out of it and given this error: The entity network ID always changes. It is never consistent, and I'm not sure why. Also note: I am trying to access singleplayer worlds exclusively, yet I am always bounced back to the multiplayer menu when getting this error. I've retried this with the last four versions of Supplementaries and a different Fabric launcher (0.17.3 instead of 0.18.3), but neither have helped the issue. Googling it hasn't helped, either-- I've seen people blame CarryOn, Origins, and the Fabric launcher itself for this happening, but none of these threads have ever reached a helpful conclusion and I'm left unsure of what to do. I'm posting this in the Supplementaries github because the error is pointing me specifically to Supplementaries being the cause. I am not sure if it truly is, or if your mod is simply triggering something that would prompt my game to blame your mod, but I'm posting here in the hopes that there is a solution to this anyways.

issues.title: [🗃]: [Supplementaries] Candle Blocks, Recursive Candle Blocks, and Candle Holders
issues.body: This feature consists of 3 key blocks: - Candle Block - Recursive Candle Block - Candle Holder **Candle Block** Crafted from 9 candles, the candle block can act as decoration, or lit if a warm block like fire, magma, or lava is above it. When lit the block starts to slowly melt away in layers like snow. Each block melts for 10 minutes, and the flame travels through pillars of candle blocks, finishing only when the last candle has burnt down fully. The candle block can be directly dyed or be crafted in all 16 colors of candle. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e73e6bf1-f34b-4cec-b40e-7dc013fe4e97) **Recursive Candle Block** The recursive candle block acts exactly like regular candle blocks with two key differences. It burns significantly faster, only taking 20 seconds to fully burn out, however once it fully burns out, the candle regenerates itself to its original height. It's fire burns blue like soul fire. **Candle Holder** The candle holder can have any candle block be placed inside of it. Once a candle block inside it fully burns out, it emits a redstone output. Pair this with the recursive candle block, it becomes a timer block, emitting a pulse after a controllable time. One recursive candle is a 20 second timer, three recursive candles lasts for a minute. Nine lasts for three minutes, etc. Since a magma block could be placed at the top of the candles to reignite them, it is automatic.

issues.title: [🗃]: Re-allow Silent Gear Arrows in Supplementaries Quiver
issues.body:
Hi,

It looks like Silent Gear has changed the way they handle their custom arrows, so that they behave more like vanilla arrows - they can no longer be 'repaired' to refresh the stack, just re-crafted:

https://github.com/SilentChaos512/Silent-Gear/issues/730
->
https://github.com/SilentChaos512/Silent-Gear/commit/8cc0ffcd75f10bd890f97396085a52193230195d

I took a look to see if this is configurable in `supplementaries-common.toml` or `supplementaries-client.toml` on my server running ATM10, but it looks like this is coded into the mod itself per:

https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/issues/860
->
https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/6e41bfdacd216d925f629b5403ddad1dc6e231d4/common/src/main/resources/data/supplementaries/tags/items/quiver_blacklist.json#L4

Therefore, I tried modifiying my copy of the Supplementaries `.jar` (`supplementaries-1.21-3.4.20-neoforge.jar`) to just replace:

`{"id":"silentgear:arrow","required":false}`
with
`{}`

in `quiver_blacklist.json`, and did a quick test - it seems to work as expected, now, at least with current(-ish) Silent Gear (`silent-gear-1.21.1-neoforge-4.0.30.jar`):

Creating a test Silent Gear arrow
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d99f5ada-2a92-425f-9ab1-43d80bfef570)

Loaded into a Supplementaries quiver
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee90124b-2876-4a08-a718-af2fd502c107)

Fired, showing the count reduce properly by one
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdbbc672-e784-4fcd-972e-14f04c859e30)

(picking the arrow up returns it to the stack inside the quiver as expected)

I'm not sure if simply emptying the list there is 100% appropriate, or if you'd want to do some kind of version check for Silent Gear >= `1.21.1-4.0.10`, but I don't believe it needs to be blacklisted any longer.  Thanks!

issues.body:
### Before Continuing:

- [x] Check you are using the latest version of the mods and its dependencies

- [x] Remove known hacky mods such as: Optifine, Fabric API/Connector on forge, and every kind of hybrid server like Mohist and Velocity. None of these are supported. Also try without other lesser usual suspects like Sodium and Lithium.
- [x] If you are unsure which mod is the culprit.
Disable all of your mods and enable them 1-2 mods each time to isolate the culprit
- [x] Confirm that there is no existing issue with a similar description submitted in the list of issues.

### Version

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Supplementaries Version

supplementaries-1.21-3.4.20-neoforge

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight-2.26.5-neoforge

### Describe Issue

**latest.log:**  https://mclo.gs/NB2hpFs
**Crash log:** https://mclo.gs/g5KZbqu

Placing a Fire Pit under a block causes the game to crash if you have the latest version of Amendments installed. This _only_ applies with the latest version of Amendments, 1.21-2.0.9, which released 4 days ago as of writing. Downgrading Amendments fixes the issue. This also only applies to placing the Fire Pit under the block; placing it on top works as expected.

The issue seems to be that the [`canSurvive`](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/master/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/common/block/blocks/FirePitBlock.java#L78) method in `FirePitBlock` references a method called [`canSurviveCeilingAndMaybeFall`](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/master/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/integration/AmendmentsCompat.java#L19) from `AmendmentsCompat`, which in turn references an identically named method in `FallingLanternEntity` in Amendments. This method was replaced with [`maybeFall`](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/amendments/blob/1.21/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/amendments/common/entity/FallingLanternEntity.java#L73) in [commit ed0494f](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/amendments/commit/ed0494f07dd88947932df13b3ce0c3a4b8e0caf3), and Supplementaries has not updated accordingly.

issues.title: [🗃]: The BIG Problem with Recipes 1.20.1
issues.body:
Short description: 
Give people freedom in terms of recipes and compatibility of the mod with others.

I ran into a big problem while making mod compatibility. Half of the recipes are dynamic. Let's take soap as an example. Soap is made from painted concrete—it's white. That's wrong; it should just be regular concrete. And because of that, people won't be able to repaint the concrete since it's already white. I'm playing with the Clayworks mod.

I'm currently improving all the dye crafting so people can repaint blocks after cleaning them, but many of the soap recipes are incorrect.

I'd add a configuration option to disable dynamic soap recipes and other things so modpack creators can create their own recipes.

issues.title: [🗃]: Master Keys
issues.body:
### The Master Key
It would be crafted like a regular key, but the gold ingot would be replaced with diamond ingot (or whatever ingot feels fitting, just not a gold one). To use it, you would shift click on an already claimed door/vault (or just use it like a regular key on unclaimed things), and it would ask the person who claimed the door (i.e. the person who used the key on the door) if they would like to be added to the master lock system. (assuming they're online, if they're not, it would say they aren't online, and to try again when they are.) If they decline, it says "Request denied", and that's that. If they accept, it says "Request accepted", and then the master key could open the doors. This could help people who manage buildings on RP servers especially if they need access to EVERY room, while certain employees could only access the doors they were allowed to. Whatever you name the Master Key would become the name of the lock system, and would show up in the description of any keys that unlock doors within that system. You could also shift click over a non-master key in your inventory to add that key specifically to the lock system instead of all the keys with that name. (Note, if you're the one who claimed the door initially, and you use a master key on it, it will say "Key(s) added to lock system!", and then you could go on with your day.)

### Version

1.20.1-FORGE

### Supplementaries Version

supplementaries-1.20.1-3.1.37

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight-1.20-2.16.5-forge

### Describe Issue

Empty cage items currently stack up to 64, despite being intended to stack [only up to 16](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/3508845b967f9379909313647ffab79cf5a44e64/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/reg/ModRegistry.java#L296). This is probably due to the `CageItem` class inheriting `AbstractMobContainerItem#getMaxStackSize`, which forces the stack size of empty cages [to be 64](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/3508845b967f9379909313647ffab79cf5a44e64/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/common/items/AbstractMobContainerItem.java#L99) in spite of the item properties given during registration.

If I'm not mistaken this should be fixable by just adding an override for `getMaxStackSize` in the `CageItem` class, but I don't have a dev environment for Supplementaries set up to test this out.

(I've also tested on 1.21.1 NeoForge using supplementaries-1.21-3.4.4 and moonlight-1.21-2.20.7, same bug occurs here as well)

issues.title: [🗃]: Make more use of the `supplementaries:sacks` item / block tags
issues.body:
Currently all item / block tags of the sack item, except for `minecraft:mineable/shear` and `supplementaries:shulker_blacklist`, are only being defined with specifically the `supplementaries:sack` item instead of the `supplementaries:sacks` tag.

I would suggest changing the remaining tags that are just being attributed to the sack item (item tag `supplementaries:overencumbering`, block tags `minecraft:guarded_by_piglins`, `supplementaries:hang_from_ropes`, `farmersdelight:mineable/knife`) to simply include the whole `supplementaries:sacks` tag, since that would make creating new sacks less error-prone for addon devs.

issues.title: [❓]: Clarification in the license regarding addons
issues.body:
### Your Question

Could the Supplementaries license be changed to clarify the status of addons?

### Detail

As of now, Version 1.3 of the Supplementaries License defines

> Compete refers to any project or software offering similar functionality, features, or services as the Software and targeting the same or a similar user base. This includes, but is not limited to, software that directly substitutes or mirrors one or more functionalities of the Software.

This, as far as I understand, could define addons for Supplementaries (even compatibility addons) as "competing" with it, since they might directly substitute or mirror functionality from Supplementaries. For example, the golden candle holders from SupplementariesSquared are mirroring a functionality (regular candle holders) from Supplementaries.

Therefore, adding clarification for addons or maybe even changing the definition of "Compete" in the license to exclude software that has a hard dependency on Supplementaries would be appreciated.

(Not related to this, but I noticed articles 4 and 5 are listed in reverse order in the current license, that should also get fixed)

issues.title: [🐞]: Logic error in `CandleHolderBlock` causing incorrect particle offsets for addons making their own candle holders
issues.body:
### Before Continuing:

- [x] Check you are using the latest version of the mods and its dependencies
- [x] Always include a latest.log if you are crashing
- [x] Remove known hacky mods such as: Optifine, Fabric API/Connector on forge, and every kind of hybrid server like Mohist and Velocity. None of these are supported. Also try without other lesser usual suspects like Sodium and Lithium.
- [x] If you are unsure which mod is the culprit.
Disable all of your mods and enable them 1-2 mods each time to isolate the culprit
- [x] Confirm that there is no existing issue with a similar description submitted in the list of issues.

### Version

1.20.1-FORGE

### Supplementaries Version

supplementaries-1.20-3.1.36.jar

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight-1.20-2.15.6-forge.jar

### Describe Issue

When an addon tries to create a subclass of `CandleHolderBlock`, the offsets for the smoke particles emitted by blocks of this subclass are incorrect if the candle holder is placed on the floor.

This is due to a check for SupplementariesSquared in [line 236](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/df4b5f51ce4a3a9d82d0d867d0e90a3b9e45a781/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/common/block/blocks/CandleHolderBlock.java#L236), which changes the offsets to accommodate for their different candle holder models based on the `private final Supplier<Boolean> isFromSuppSquared` attribute.

However, instead of checking whether a given candle holder is from SupplementariesSquared, this Supplier actually just returns if it [isn't from Supplementaries](https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/blob/df4b5f51ce4a3a9d82d0d867d0e90a3b9e45a781/common/src/main/java/net/mehvahdjukaar/supplementaries/common/block/blocks/CandleHolderBlock.java#L70C13-L70C79). This means it always returns true for _any_ addon, instead of just for SupplementariesSquared.

Circumventing this issue from the addon side isn't really feasible (without using mixins), as it requires access to the private `PARTICLE_OFFSETS` attribute of `CandleHolderBlock`. Of course one could just copy the source code, but that would be bad coding practice and not ideal from a licensing point of view.

Thus, I would appreciate changing `isFromSuppSquared` to output values correctly, and / or changing the `PARTICLE_OFFSETS` attribute to just be protected or public instead of private so they can be adjusted by addons devs directly without the need for mixins.

**Hello, the quiver in this mod is a highly practical tool accessory, but it could be made even better. In my modpack, the following issues have occurred:**

issues.body: Minecraft: 1.21.1 NeoForge: 21.1.193 Mods: - Supplementaries [1.21-3.3.5] - Continuity [3.0.0+1.21.neoforge] - Forgified Fabric API [0.115.6+2.1.1+1.21.1] - More Red [6.0.0.3] - Resourceful Lib [3.0.12] - Sinytra Connector [2.0.0-beta.8+1.21.1] Expected behavior: Wires from the More Red mod connect when placed adjacent to each other, as seen in the image below. This behavior remains normal if either Continuity or Supplementaries are installed separately alongside More Red. Resultant Behavior: When both Supplementaries and Continuity are installed with More Red, the connected textures break, causing the connections between wires to not be rendered. Note that they are still functionally connected, as shown by their hitboxes. Logs: https://gist.github.com/CraftyZombie/8a46f4699214731e118dd3ffd846b99f Note: A very similar conflict occurs between More Red, Continuity, and Bumblezone, which can be seen in this report: https://github.com/Commoble/morered/issues/51

issues.title: [❓]: Modded/Non-Vanilla Mob Flute Summoning
issues.body:
### Your Question

Is it possible to get full compatibility with additional mobs being summoned by the flute?

### Detail

Hello!  I am currently working on a modpack which includes both Supplementaries and Domestication Innovation.  DI adds several vanilla mobs to the tamable list, including frogs, axolotls, and rabbits.  By adding the `flute_pet` tag to these mobs, I was able to bind them to the flute to be summoned to the player.  However, they are only being summoned when bound, whereas an unbound flute seems to be summoning only tamed cats and dogs, not any other mobs (even ones that can be tamed in vanilla, like horses).  Is there a way to make it so flutes will summon any pet of which you are the owner?  Or is that not something Supplementaries currently has an option for?

- [x] Confirm that there is no existing issue with a similar description submitted in the list of issues.

### Version

1.21.1-NEOFORGE

### Supplementaries Version

supplementaries-1.21-3.3.5-neoforge

### Moonlight Lib Version

moonlight-1.21-2.19.5-neoforge

### Describe Issue

After placing books in the world, trying to remove one of them individually (with shift + rightclick) instead causes the placed books to both start becoming invisible and/or the amount of shown books starts showing a lower amount, despite the player not (necessarily) getting any actual book back. When the stack is broken, not all books will be present.

E.g. place 4 books in one block, shift + RMB to take 1 or a couple, not obtain any books into inventory, while breaking the remaining stack might give 3 instead of 4 (even when trying to take multiple), or less. It's fairly vague in how many less there will be, but very consistent in that it deletes books - they won't be in the placed stack anymore (even when broken), nor in player's inventory, nor on the ground, even after reloading the world/game.

I'm not sure if the shift + RMB shortcut is even meant to be an intended way to take individual books, but it's a key combo that seems to come natural to people to try and thus if it's not intended to work, at least it should not be deleting books.

Could reproduce in a clean NeoForge 1.21.1 instance with no other mods present (just `supplementaries-1.21-3.3.5-neoforge` + `moonlight-1.21-2.19.5-neoforge`), tried it with first release candidate of the mod too (so `supplementaries-1.21-3.1.0-neoforge` + `moonlight-1.21-2.18.2-neoforge` + `create-1.21.1-6.0.0`) to confirm the issue is not something relatively new, and even could reproduce in a clean Fabric 1.21.1 install (so with `supplementaries-1.21-3.3.5-fabric` + `moonlight-1.21-2.19.5-fabric` + `fabric-api-0.116.4+1.21.1`).

I also made a bug report in the Discord server #bugs-and-issues channel in case you prefer that, I linked the two issue posts to each other for convenience, here's the post in discord: https://discord.com/channels/790151253144895508/1393690303197745153/1393690303197745153

issues.title: [❓]: Simple flower box modded compat
issues.body:
### Your Question

Is there any way to add compatibility for other tall flowers from other mods?

### Detail

I've looked through the customization wiki and haven't found anything, i was just wondering if there was a way to let tall flowers from other mods be placed in simple flower boxes. If not, is it in the realm of possibility to add it as a feature?

### Version

1.20.1-FORGE

### Supplementaries Version

Supplementaries 1.20-3.1.18

### Moonlight Lib Version

Moonlight 1.20-2.13.81

### Describe Issue

When I'm out in the world, I will sometimes hear this one music disc, Pancake from Supplementaries mod, play randomly. It is not positional, it sounds like it's coming from everywhere, and it disappears immediately after I set the jukebox music sounds to 0 and then back up. I'm not sure if this is a Sophisticated Backpacks issue or a Supplementaries issue, so I'm inquiring into both.

Version & Mods
• 1.20.1 Forge, Java Edition
• Sophisticated Backpacks
• Supplementaries
• Supplementaries Squared

Steps
1. Exist in the world
2. Occasionally everyone on the server will just start hearing Pancake play as an ambient sound that does not seem to be coming from anywhere
3. Turning my jukebox sounds off and on again stops the disc only for me.
4. Waiting out the disc usually results in it cutting itself off randomly in the middle.
5. I have never found a mob with a backpack from Sophisticated Backpacks nearby while this disc was heard playing.
6. It may be possible that moving away from where you first heard the sound can cause it to cut off, but this is unverified.

Expectations
1. To not hear random phantom music discs that happen as server-wide events but can be dismissed through client-side actions

Again, I don't know if this is a Sophisticated Backpacks issue or a Supplementaries issue, but when I first heard the disc, I thought it was a backpack until I dug around and found no backpacks within range. I can also provide the full modpack we're using in case there's some API in there that's causing this weird phenomenon.

issues.title: [🐞]: Supplementaries incompatible with Create 0.5.1.j
issues.body:
Edit:
Supplementaries made changes that broke compatibility with versions prior to 6.x of Create.
Nowhere is this documented, leaving users to guess which of the latest versions predate this change. 
This in particular causes issues for users who allowed mod managers to update their mods. 

Supplementaries does not list an incompatibility in any relevant changelog, nor a requirement of 6.0 in a way (not even as an optional) that mod sites can recognize - a feature commonly taken advantage of on sites like Curse and Modrinth in particular.

This is problematic in particular for those trying to manage a server modpack. Create's big leap in changes from 5.x to 6.x has left a gap in support among the Create community, meaning some core addons have yet to update forcing modpackers to remain on the older Create version until updates are made, lest they break the modpack entirely.

A simple mention of this in a changelog would have avoided confusion and helped find an appropriate version predating this issue, without having to resort to trial and error, loading each latest version until one was found that didn't refuse to load.

### Before Continuing:

- [x] Check you are using the latest version of the mods and its dependencies
- [x] Always include a latest.log if you are crashing
- [x] Remove mod that enhances Minecraft: Optifine, Sodium, others. The issue persists.
- [x] If you are unsure which mod is the culprit.
Disable all of your mods and enable them 1-2 mods each time to isolate the culprit
- [x] Confirm that there is no existing issue with a similar description submitted in the list of issues.

### Version

1.20.1-FORGE

### Supplementaries Version

3.1.29 

### Moonlight Lib Version

1.20-2.14.0-forge

### Describe Issue

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba65ab84-dc2c-4823-9b96-45f696f813a8)
Not to be confused with issue https://github.com/MehVahdJukaar/Supplementaries/issues/1450

Supplementaries causes dependency related crash, stating incompatibility with Create 0.5.1.j

### Observation:
Examining the mod files and the modpage, Supplementaries is: 

- not listed as a Create mod, nor is Create mentioned
- does not list Create as a dependency on it's mod page on Modrinth or Curseforge
- does not list supported version of Create in any current or recent versions of Supplementaries on ModRinth or Curseforge
- does not list anything regarding Create in the mods.toml

### The problem
There is no obvious way to foresee this dependency without triggering a crash, if the user is not using Create 6.0.0
Many users are still on 0.5.1.j or earlier due to early adoption phase of users and mod authors.
Dependencies should always be clearly noted.
No documentation of the dependency means users are left to brute force guess by downloading multiple versions until they find one that doesn't crash the game over the dependency.

Given that Create 6.0.0 is not listed as a hard dependency:
This may be the result of an indirect issue, where optional integration of Create 6.0.0 causes a non-graceful failure (crash), instead of ignoring the outdated version.

### Recommendation
Update relevant sections of modpage, mods.toml and version uploads to treat this as a dependency on 6.0.0 for an optional features, or as a hard incompatibility with earlier versions.
This could help users find a version that will not fail to load, and avoid confusing users with a dependency crash in the absence of a hard dependency
or
add safeguard checks to check if an older version of Create is present. Have features dependent on Create 6.0.0 default to simpler non-dependent behaviors/features or disabled them entirely.

issues.title: [🗃]: More Sliding Block Parts
issues.body:
Just a couple of ideas I had concerning the Sliding Block and its functionality.

New Blocks/Parts

Movement Pads: Arrow block. When a Sliding Block is pushed or falls onto one, it's pushed one tile in the direction of the block's arrow. Does not move players.
Heavy Switch: Sliding Block-specific switch. When a Sliding Block is pushed onto this 2-tall block, the top half will sink into the bottom half, like a piston, and the bottom half will emit a redstone signal once it's fully retracted. Resets when the block is removed.

New Mechanics
Smooth stone can be "etched" with a hammer and chisel to make channels to push a sliding block in, effectively constraining its movement to a track. These tracks can curve.
Sliding Blocks can contain a single stack of items, but said items can only be accessed via item-transfer mechanics (no direct inventory access)
